summary: Phase 149O.20J.5 -- Class-B ACL-Only Higher-Ancestor Detection Narrow Repair (macOS): repaired B-149O.20J.4-1, the Blocking finding disclosed (not repaired) by 149O.20J.4. _acl_grants_agent_write_macos gated ACL-presence detection on a '+' marker in `ls -lde`'s mode column, then searched for the literal substring "write" -- both independently wrong on a real host. Empirically confirmed on this real macOS 26.6.1 (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64) host via real chmod +a grants: modern macOS attaches a com.apple.provenance extended attribute to effectively every filesystem object (confirmed via xattr -l, confirmed non-removable), which renders the trailing mode-column marker '@' instead of '+' even when a real ACL coexists, so the pre-repair '+'-gate silently discarded real ACL evidence before the substring search ever ran; and macOS canonicalizes directory-replacement rights to add_file/add_subdirectory/delete_child (none of which contain 'write'). Reproduced B-149O.20J.4-1 against the exact pre-repair blob (git show 0b2fd134:src/pcae/core/hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py, not retyped) with a real chmod +a add_file,delete_child grant, isolated at /private/tmp to avoid the /tmp-symlink confound: _ancestor_chain_safe returned safe=True, reaching the filesystem root, despite a ground-truth-verified (real touch-in-directory probe) ACL-writable grandparent. Independently re-derived the macOS ACL canonical output grammar from real chmod +a grants rather than assuming man chmod's prose or the token passed to chmod +a: numbered ACL entry lines of the form ' N: <principal> allow|deny <right1,right2,...>', principal as user:<name>/group:<name>; discovered write(file)/add_file(dir) and append(file)/add_subdirectory(dir) are the identical underlying NFSv4 ACE bit rendered contextually by ls, so a single unified rights vocabulary works for both files and directories without branching on path.is_dir(); delete/writeattr/writeextattr render identically in both contexts; delete_child is directory-only. Rewrote _acl_grants_agent_write_macos (signature widened to accept agent_uid/agent_gids, matching the Linux sibling) to parse the numbered entry lines directly (never gating on the marker character), resolve principal identity via pwd.getpwnam/grp.getgrnam (imported locally inside the macOS-only function to preserve cross-platform top-level import safety), and classify rights against an explicit known-rights vocabulary (write/append/writeattr/writeextattr/add_file/add_subdirectory/delete_child/delete as write-capable; read/execute/readattr/readextattr/readsecurity/list/search/chown/writesecurity/the four inherit flags as known-safe) -- any right token outside that union fails closed (None), never silently treated as non-write; malformed entry lines fail closed; deny entries are parsed for malformed/unrecognized-token detection but never contribute a grant; an unresolvable principal on a write-capable allow entry fails closed (indeterminate), never a silent non-match. Updated _acl_grants_agent_write's darwin branch to pass agent identity through. No other function's signature or behavior changed; _ancestor_chain_safe, _effective_write_access, _resolve_trusted_executable, _resolve_trusted_executable_with_effective_access, and the Linux ACL path are byte-unchanged. Disclosed a deliberate simplification: full NFSv4 first-entry-wins deny-precedence evaluation is not implemented -- any allow entry granting a write-capable right to a matching principal is treated as writable regardless of a later deny entry that might technically override it under strict NFSv4 semantics; this can only cause an over-cautious classification, never mask a real grant. Added tests/test_phase_149o_20j_5_class_b_acl_only_higher_ancestor_detection_macos_narrow_repair.py: 39 new tests, all real-ACL-backed (zero mocked ACL primitive calls in the positive-detection tests), run twice for determinism with identical results, covering: historical pre-repair reproduction from the fixed 0b2fd134 blob; each directory right (add_file/add_subdirectory/delete_child/delete) individually ground-truth-verified via a right-specific probe (create-file/create-subdirectory/delete-preexisting-child/rename-self respectively, since each right authorizes a narrower action than a generic touch probe would prove); combined canonicalized multi-right grants (the exact output after one chmod +a call, not three separate grants); POSIX-safe control; file-level write/append/writeextattr; irrelevant-rights-only entries; unrelated-user principal; effective-group principal (everyone, gid 12, a real -- not special-cased -- group match since macOS includes gid 12 in every process's supplementary groups); deny-not-treated-as-allow; malformed ACL output; unexpected right token; ACL-tool-unavailable; subprocess error; unresolvable write-capable principal; full ancestor-chain composition at one and two levels above a safe parent; fully-safe-chain control; Trusted-Git composition; Protected-Root composition; Git/Protected-Root equivalence on the identical real-ACL attack; early-stop-repair regression (both directions); J-1/J-2/J-3 regressions; symlinked-higher-ancestor regression; indeterminate-ACL-above-safe-ancestor fail-closed; read-only wall; zero production consumers; HMIC frozen-set unchanged (25/5); production-scope-limited-to-topology-verifier; real-host NON_COMPLIANT. Removed the two strict=True xfail markers in 149O.20J.4's own suite (test_acl_only_higher_ancestor_write_macos, test_acl_grants_agent_write_macos_direct_ground_truth) whose own reason text explicitly pre-authorized removal 'once a follow-up phase repairs the ACL right-name matching and this test genuinely passes' -- this is that phase; a disclosed, pre-authorized contract evolution, not a silent rewrite, with the underlying pytest.fail-on-True assertions converted to direct positive assert statements. No other assertion in that file was changed. ADJUDICATED J-3's historical closure: the original B-CBV-J-3 defect text explicitly named ancestor-level ACL blindness ('...git executable, its ancestors, or a PATH-preceding directory would not be detected'), and 149O.20J.1's repair explicitly claimed ancestor-ACL coverage as part of its closure ('both the Git executable ACL and Git ancestor ACL requirements... are covered by this single composition'). 149O.20J.2's independent verification of that specific claim used only simulated/forced ACL results ('with the ACL sub-check forced to report no ACL', 'simulated an ACL-only write grant'), never a real chmod +a grant. This phase's real-host evidence shows the underlying primitive did not correctly recognize real canonical directory rights at the time of that closure. Verdict: OUTCOME B -- the historical closure was broader than the evidence justified for its specific ancestor-ACL-coverage sub-claim; narrowed (not rewritten): J-3's core delegation-wiring defect (ACL now consulted at all, for both the executable's own bytes and its ancestor chain, via the shared primitives) remains INDEPENDENTLY CLOSED, re-confirmed end-to-end with a fresh real file-level ACL grant on a would-be trusted executable; the specific real-macOS-evidence gap in what that delegation relied on is exactly B-149O.20J.4-1, now repaired by this phase. No historical test file's assertions were deleted or retyped to match this narrowing -- 149O.20J.1/.2's own documents remain the unedited historical record; this phase's own document records the adjudication. Governed lifecycle: closed the stale idle placeholder task, opened a fresh governed task 20260812-2046-phase-149o-20j-5-... with hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py newly allowed (repair phase, unlike J.4's verification-only scope) and the other two Class-B modules plus HMIC-adjacent modules explicitly forbidden. Committed via `pcae commit implementation` (commit 6a265e09) -- staged-file-aware, no raw git commit, no --no-verify, no force push. Post-commit fast_green (pytest -m fast_green -n auto, --ignore for the two pre-existing non-deterministic-collection files -- fido2 module absent, and a UUID-parametrized test whose IDs vary per collecting process, both confirmed pre-existing and unrelated by reproducing the identical failure on the stashed clean baseline before this phase's changes existed): 71 failed / 6771 passed / 5 skipped, byte-identical in count to 149O.20J.4's own citation, zero of the 71 in this phase's test files. Post-commit broad sweep (pytest -k 'class_b or hbdc or 149o_20j' -n auto): 11 failed / 658 passed / 5 skipped / 1 pre-existing collection error, identical failure count and identical failing node IDs to the clean pre-phase baseline (re-verified via git stash -u before this phase's changes existed) -- zero delta attributable to this phase; the higher 'passed' count (658 vs baseline 617) reflects this phase's 39 new tests plus the 2 formerly-xfailed J.4 tests now genuinely passing. B-149O.20J.4-1: REPAIRED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING -- NOT CLOSED (not independently closed in this same phase, per the governing prompt). CBV-S1: OPEN -- HMIC SOURCE-SCOPE BINDING STILL PENDING. CBV-S10: OPEN -- READINESS CONTRACT/INTEGRATION GAP, unchanged. Class-B: CONTRACT VERIFIED -- ACL REPAIR IMPLEMENTED NON-AUTHORITATIVELY -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING -- NOT PROVISIONED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. Real host remains deliberately unprovisioned: verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() returns NON_COMPLIANT, confirmed both before and after this phase's changes. HMIC frozen scope unchanged: _FROZEN_AUTHORITY_BEARING_FILES still exactly 25 entries (none of the three Class-B modules present), _CONTRACT_IDENTITY_FILES still exactly 5 members. Zero production consumers of any of the three Class-B modules (git grep-confirmed). Read-only/no-mutation wall reconfirmed via source inspection. Production diff scope confirmed via git diff --name-only 0b2fd134 -- src/: exactly hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py. Wrote docs/PHASE_149O_20J_5_CLASS_B_ACL_ONLY_HIGHER_ANCESTOR_DETECTION_NARROW_REPAIR.md documenting methodology, real ACL canonicalization derivation, HBDC right-classification derivation, the implementation diff, full regression results, the J-3 scope adjudication, and all status confirmations. Updated PROJECT_STATUS.md (demoting 149O.20J.4 to a new stacked Previous Phase entry) and CHANGELOG.md. Recommended next phase: Phase 149O.20J.6 -- Class-B macOS ACL-Only Higher-Ancestor Detection Repair Independent Verification -- must independently re-derive HBDC-REQ-016/017/020 and the macOS ACL canonicalization grammar from primary evidence rather than assuming this phase's own derivation, and independently reproduce this phase's real-ACL test results, before B-149O.20J.4-1 may be considered for closure. 149O.20K (HMIC Class-B Verifier Source-Scope Contract Evolution) must not begin until 149O.20J.6 passes, and must still perform its own fresh HMIC-REQ-052 transitive authority-dependency closure analysis rather than assuming the HMIC source count changes.
